premise.claim: Changing spec.worker.tieredStore on an existing CacheRuntime updates the runtime ConfigMap but not the worker Pod. The quota ends up recorded as two different values, and no event, condition or log line says so. (issue #6192, OPEN, re-checked 2026-11-27)
premise.patchedComponent: pkg/ddc/cache/engine (sync.go, status.go, util.go, setup.go) + api/v1alpha1/status.go + pkg/common/constants.go + docs
premise.evidence: results/r8-premise-base-b8ff60e3.txt: on the round-8 base b8ff60e3 the ConfigMap quota follows the edited spec (16Gi) while the worker ASTS volume keeps 8Gi, with 0 events and no tieredStore condition (TestVerifyPR6219R8Premise_SilentOnBase PASS on base). On head d19969af the same canary flips: full Sync emits 'Warning RuntimeTieredStoreConflict Worker tieredStore cannot be updated in-place after creation: worker pod volume tiered-store-level-0-memory differs from spec tieredStore. Delete and recreate the CacheRuntime to apply changes.' and persists TieredStoreSynced=False (results/r8-unit-head-d19969af.txt). Round-7 base 253f6bb8 verdict carried: confirmed (results/base-premise-unit.txt).

findings.note: Flips red on head = the drift is no longer silent (fix working). Passes on base (premise reproduction).
Both trees: ConfigMap follows the edited spec while the pod volume keeps the creation-time size; the PR warns instead of patching volumes, and #6299 (OPEN) tracks the ConfigMap side.
TS-REMEDIATION-GUIDANCE-WEDGE: genuine drift keeps 'Delete and recreate the CacheRuntime to apply changes.'; invalid specs must NOT advise recreate (covered by TS-DISPATCH-PRECEDENCE tests).
TS-DOC-CLIENT-SCOPE: docs stay worker-scoped; client-side silence tracked in #6221 (OPEN, re-checked 2026-11-27).
Tripwire for the #6221 deferral: STILL-PRESENT (passing) is the expected state until client-side drift detection lands; a flip means the deferral ended and the docs/tests must be revisited.

Contract restated in round 8: a multi-medium level is now a transform error surfaced as RuntimeTieredStoreInvalid (never a precedence race against pod volumes). The rounds 2-3 order-matching form is archived in attic/.

Round-7 blocker, fixed in round 8 by matching the exact generated shape (tiered-store-level-<N>-index-<M> / -memory) via isGeneratedTieredStoreVolumeName; user/class volumes sharing the bare prefix are ignored, genuine generated-shape orphans are still flagged, and the transform-name invariant guards the want/got filter asymmetry.

Carried rounds 2-7 advisory, resolved by design in round 8: the persistent TieredStoreSynced condition is the durable record (survives event TTL and controller restarts, needs no requeue), and events are transition-only. Envtest proves restart-proof dedup against a real API server.

NEW in round 8 (minor): a persisted TieredStoreSynced=False is never re-evaluated once spec.worker.disabled=true skips the worker branch, so a stale conflict alarm (with recreate advice) outlives the worker. Canary passes while stale; flips when the disabled path clears or marks the condition Unknown.
Docs claim hostPath.quotas/high/low edits are ConfigMap-only and never warn.
